wa_main_wall_the.blurb: The largest wall at Deep Creek, a basalt canyon in the Spokane area, and a destination for strong sport climbers. All 26 routes are bolted, and the grades sit well toward the hard end: one 5.10, a handful of 5.11s, then a big block of 5.12 and 5.13 with a couple of 5.14 lines at the top. The wall overhangs steeply on columnar basalt, so expect powerful, pumpy climbing rather than slabs. Routes are described as well protected, and many chains are set up for lowering. Rain does little to the main face, which makes it handy in unsettled weather. Early in the year, high creek water can cut off the left side of the wall. Not a place for beginners.

wa_pearly_gates.blurb: A shaded crag above Snow Creek in Icicle Canyon near Leavenworth, mostly one or two pitches of crack and slab climbing. Of the 27 routes, most are trad and a few are bolted, with grades running from the 5.7 range through a solid middle of 5.9 and 5.10 and a few 5.11s and one 5.12 above. The granite is fine grained and grippy, and the wall faces north, which makes it a good summer pick when sunnier walls bake. The walk in is the main cost: a steep climber's trail with a log crossing of the creek, taking roughly half an hour or more. Bring a standard rack for the crack lines.
wa_pearly_gates.parking_note: Leave the car in the Snow Creek trailhead lot on the left side of Icicle Road, a few miles up the canyon from the edge of Leavenworth.
wa_pearly_gates.approach: From the lot, follow the Snow Creek trail briefly, then take the climber's trail that branches right. It crosses the braided creek on logs and then climbs steeply through forest to the base, gaining roughly 1,000 feet.

wa_tin_man.blurb: A bouldering area high up Icicle Creek outside Leavenworth, set in forest with dappled light. The 27 problems cover a wide spread: a good number of V0 to V3 lines for newer boulderers, a few V4 and V5 problems, and several V6 and V7 tests at the top. The walk in follows an unmarked path with a short scramble over uneven rocks, so it feels secluded. Plan on more than one pad and a spotter, as the ground can be rough. Warm summer months are the most comfortable time to visit, while winter brings snow and the shoulder seasons are unpredictable.
